content.title: About
content.content: Baked beans are canned beans cooked in a tomato‑based sauce without any meat. The vegetarian version contains only beans, tomatoes, spices and sometimes a small amount of vegetable oil. Beans are rich in plant protein, fiber and complex carbohydrates, making them a filling and nutritious dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans are one of the oldest cultivated crops, with evidence of use dating back over 7,000 years.
Tomatoes in the sauce give baked beans their characteristic sweet‑tart flavor and add lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Vegetarian baked beans are a staple in traditional British meals such as the full English breakfast.
Different bean varieties (white, kidney, pinto) are used, each offering a distinct taste and texture.
Canning preserves beans for several years while retaining most of their nutrients.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A typical serving (≈130 g) provides about 7 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar levels, and promotes heart health.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Beans contain iron for blood formation and folate, which is essential during pregnancy.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Complex carbs raise blood glucose slowly, beneficial for weight management and diabetes control.

items.title: Tomato antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene and vitamin C in the sauce protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned beans often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytates, which can reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in excess.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause flatulence in sensitive people; increase intake gradually.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked beans can be served hot as a side dish, added to chili, soups, salads, or used in vegetarian burger patties. They are easy to reheat in the microwave or on the stove and pair well with whole‑grain toast or mashed potatoes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer the beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 5 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
